we introduce Spider, which consists of 200 databases with multiple tables, 10,181 questions, and 5,693 corresponding complex SQL queries, all written by 11 college students spending a total of 1,000 man-hours
Most of the previous work train their models without schemas as inputs because they use a single database for both training and testing.
All questions and SQL queries were written and reviewed by 11 computer science students.
we develop our dataset in five steps, spending around 1,000 hours of human labor in total
Our 200 databases covering 138 different domains are collected from three resources.
First, we collected about 70 complex databases from different college database courses, SQL tutorial websites, online csv files, and textbook examples.
Finally, we created the remaining 90 databases based on WikiSQL.
For example, 'student id' might be represented by 'stu id'.
For each database, we ask eight computer science students proficient in SQL to create 20-50 natural questions and their SQL labels.
we did not use any template or script to generate question and SQL queries
SELECT with multiple columns and aggregations, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT, JOIN, INTERSECT, EXCEPT, UNION, NOT IN, OR, AND, EXISTS, LIKE as well as nested queries
we did not create questions that are (1) vague or too ambiguous, or (2) require knowledge outside the database to answer
Once the database is labeled with question-query pairs, we ask a different annotator to check if the questions are clear and contain enough information to answer the query.
After SQL labels are reviewed, native English speakers review and correct each question.
Also, we run a script to execute and parse all SQL labels to make sure they are correct.
Spider has 200 distinct databases covering 138 different domains such as college, club, TV show, government, etc.
Most domains have one database, thus containing 20-50 questions
On average, each database in Spider has 27.6 columns and 8.8 foreign keys.
Spider contains about twice more nested queries and 10 times more ORDER BY

Spider is a large-scale complex and cross-domain semantic parsing and text-to-SQL dataset annotated by 11 Yale students.
It consists of 10,181 questions and 5,693 unique complex SQL queries on 200 databases with multiple tables covering 138 different domains.
To do well on it, systems must generalize well to not only new SQL queries but also new database schemas
But all SQL queries are simple, and each database is only a simple table without any foreign key.
Each of them contains only a single database with a limited number of SQL queries, and has exact same SQL queries in train and test splits.
